LEGO Technic Stunt Show Truck & Bike 42106; Includes Stunt Motorcycle, Toy Truck and Trailer (P10 Pieces) LEGO Technic is very different from regular LEGO blocks, even though they can combine, but the difference is strong enough that this will be a very different type of challenge for young builders. text_fidelity_a:
Loopdedoo – DIY Friendship Bracelet Maker Kit – Make Bracelets in Minutes – Award-Winning Craft Kit - Ages 8+ It's suggested for ages 8 and older, and I'd agree with that age range. I think younger kids could successfully use it if an older, experience person was nearby to help. Basically, you loop embroidery thread around the two hooks to create the desired core thickness, then twist a knob to spin the core while you lay down an outer design over that core. You tie on the finished piece using the end loops. The bracelet should withstand normal wear if tied according to the directions.

The distance from one hook to the other is 11", but longer items can be made by linking finished 11" pieces or by a somewhat trickier shifting of the piece after you have 11" of it's length finished. You can, of course, make lengths shorter than 11". The instructional book was easy to follow and was all I needed to create a nice bracelet with no frustration involved. They also have good instructional videos on their website: annwilliamsgroup. com/instructional-videos

Included in the kit is the main Loopdedoo tool (with a push-out drawer for storing the thread and clips); instructional booklet; 18 skeins of embroidery thread (100% cotton, 8.7 yards) in a variety of colors including reds through purples, black, brown, and cream; and 2 alligator clips (which are used with the tool to hold threads in place when making the longer items). The thread is Made in China, but I think the loop Loopdedoo is made in the USA.

I hope to use this tool with a group of middle grade girls soon as I think they'll get a kick out of it. The Loopdedoo is made from a solid plastic that feels like it will last. Is this fairly simplistic tool worth price? Well, if the person it's intended for will only make a few bracelets and then move on to the next toy, then probably not. But if she loves to make her own, unique bracelets and tends to continue with an activity she enjoys, then this might be a good tool to support her creativity.
text_fidelity_b: Loopdedoo – DIY Friendship Bracelet Maker Kit – Make Bracelets in Minutes – Award-Winning Craft Kit - Ages 8+

Happily, the conductor has a hole on the bottom that can be used to tighten or loosen the bolts. My three-year-old niece was content with using this as is and loves the train so much as a toy that I'll give it 3 stars, but I think many children would prefer the fun of the motorized drill. When you press a button, the train makes a chu-chu sound and a very dim white light comes out the front. You can't see the light unless you're looking for it. The "design and drill" is basically some bolts to screw on to hold the covers and the wheels in place. There were several colors of bolts you can choose from to make different "designs."

The engine measures 10 inches long by 6 inches wide by 6 inches tall. The wagon measures 7.5 inches long by 6 inches wide by 3.75 inches tall. The wagon bed is 2 inches deep. The caboose measures 7.5 inches long 6 inches wide and 5 inches tall. Three AAA batteries are needed to power the drill according to the instruction manual, and two AAA batteries are needed for the train engine for the sound and light. The wheels roll smoothly and securely, and it is easy to connect the three sections of the train together, so it is a good toy not just a building activity. There are some extra bolts in case some are lost. The train is sturdy and can withstand the rough treatment of a 3-year-old armed with a plastic hammer.

text_fidelity_a:
LEGO Creator Expert 10253 Big Ben Building Kit As will become clear in this review, I am a true fan of Lego. Does that bias my review? I dont think so, you may disagree...

This is a big set. This is not a set for your younger Lego builders, not because its too hard, but because some of it will become tedious to younger minds. But us older people refusing to grow up (46 and still building with Lego!) will love this. There are several points during the build where you think "Oh WOW, thats clever" - very good.
The end result is bigger than I expected. Most of my recent large set builds have been the modular Lego City sets, which are built the right size for Lego Minifigs - this is much smaller than that! So you cannot add it to your Lego City, but you can have it in the back ground.

Its about an 8 hour build. The manual is excellent, but with less writing than some of the other ones - the Lego Eiffel Tower's Manual had a lot more information on the history of the Tower. This has a few snippets about the history, the Big Ben bell, but more would have been appreciated.

When finished, it is beautiful. You can turn the knob on the back to adjust the time - you cannot really adjust the time - the hour and minute hand are tuck, so as one turns, so does the other. But its still awesome!
The tree outside the main entrance is wonderful! one of my favorite parts of the build!

I believe that Lego is the best toy ever made. This set only re-enforces that opinion. Some Legos, when complete can be played with (the Lego City ones, for instance) but others not so much. I dont see this being played with, just built, displayed, and maybe dismantled and rebuilt.

5 stars though. A wonderful Lego set. A must have for collectors big kids, and us huge kids!
text_fidelity_b: LEGO Creator Expert 10253 Big Ben Building Kit

text_fidelity_a:
3Doodler Start Essentials 3D Pen Set For Kids with Free Refill Filament - STEM Toy For Boys & Girls, Age 6 & Up - Toy of The Year Award Winner I think this thing is awesome!

That said, I do have a couple of warnings to consider. First, it will get really expensive! The sticks don't go very far at all. (The package claims each 6 inch stick will give you 60 inches of play, so I'm going to assume we just need more practice to get that much, as I'm guessing most others will, too.) With this set, you'll get 2 packs of the sticks(48 total sticks...6 each of white, mint green, yellow, orange, blue, red, green, and grey). You'll use those up super quick! These sticks are biodegradable, BPA-free and labeled as "safe". From what I've read, you'll need these specific sticks to go with the 3Doodler.

Also, every time you put a new color stick through the pen, you'll be wasting a bit of the previous stick, unless it works into your design. The whole stick won't completely feed through until you put another one in there to push it on out.

It takes a great deal of practice to get anything worthwhile to turn out. I have 3 little boys and they all want a chance at practicing, so even more sticks are used up in that process. So far, we haven't came up with anything close to what is shown in the practice book, but none of us can call ourselves overly skilled in the artistic realm at this point in time.

All of that said, IF your budget allows for buying lots of sticks to go with this pen, it truly is awesome! (Or you could request packs of these sticks as grandparent presents for the kids.) ;) Letting a child use his/her imagination with this thing is an amazing opportunity, and I definitely recommend it. (I even recommend it for adults, too, because we all need a little childish fun every once in awhile!)

It's easy to use. Just charge it up with the included micro USB cable(or do like me and use your kindle charger), turn it on and wait for the light to turn green. Then, press the button to start it and press it again to stop it. Simple! As I mentioned earlier, there is a book with instructions and some ideas to practice and get started with the pen. There's no worries about getting burned. I tested it out, and while the plastic is a little warm when it first comes out, it's not even close to hot. This allows for a little wiggle room for moving around your design before it completely dries.

In the end, other than the sticks being a costly investment, this is a great little invention, and we've loved it so far!
text_fidelity_b: 3Doodler Start Essentials 3D Pen Set For Kids with Free Refill Filament - STEM Toy For Boys & Girls, Age 6 & Up - Toy of The Year Award Winner

text_fidelity_a:
Discover with Dr. Cool PRO Series Rock Tumbler - Turn Rocks into Stunning Gemstones! At first I put this in the kitchen, I quickly learned that it was too loud for an open floor plan, it made me listen to tv on too high of a volume, so when I switched to the 2nd grit I moved it to a spare bedroom. This worked out great since I go in that room almost daily I was able to keep up with knowing when to change out to the next grit.

This is super easy to set up and get started. It comes with absolutely everything needed to go from start to finish including jewelry items to use so you can show off your stones. The instructions are very easy to follow along too.It also comes with activity books and the jewelry pieces are a necklace, a ring, a keychain and ear rings.

The instructions gives you an idea of how long the stones should tumble in each grit and at what speed.
This is what I did..
-grit #1..I did for 3 days on #3 speed
-grit#2.. I started at 5 days on #2…then opened it up and decided it needed a few more days since they were a bit rough so I did 2
more days on #3 setting
-grit#3.. I did for 7 days on #1 setting.
-grit#4..I did 7 days on #1. The smaller stones were great , the larger stones had a few blemishes yet, but I like things when they

This is no exception. The pieces fit well together, they also arrive in good condition, and hold up well to adult assembly. I put things to the test when I spilled a bit of scotch (fortunately not a single malt) all over the puzzle! This puzzle isn't the most complex, but the scenery is gorgeous (albeit a work of art not a real moment of nature). It came together over a few evenings (with the help or perhaps hindrance of the aforementioned scotch).

I didn't test the augmented reality due to not having an iOS device (not really that appealing to me anyway, but I do applaud Ravensburger for trying something new). I did get a bit annoyed with the fact that the large image of the completed work on the box top was obscured by an image of the augmented reality in use. This made assembling the bottom left a bit more difficult than necessary. Feel free to try new things, but let's not interfere with good ole fashioned puzzle making!

text_fidelity_a:
Fisher-Price Roar 'n Ride Lion [[VIDEOID:6d6cbfe820d25c4bf20272caa9cdc5e0]] My girlfriend said, "This is the kind of toy that you only get for your worst enemies." I, on the other hand love it! And, kids love it too. The problem with this is that it's a noise-making toy that is very fun and exciting if you're the one controlling it, but kind of annoying if you're not controlling it.

This is a play lion, that comes with suction cups to stick to the side of the car. When you press the lion's belly, then it makes some sounds. When you rattle something, like with the attached rattle, then it does extended music and sound. It's meant to teach kids that if they rattle something, then something else in the environment might react.

One big warning. This ships in Demo mode, where pressing the Lion's tummy works, but the rattle doesn't work. At first I thought it was broken. But, all you have to do is switch this off and then switch it back on, and then both the rattle and pressing the Lion's abdomen will work. And, speaking of switching this off, the switch is hidden on the lion's back, and is super hard to get to. And, it's impossible to change the batteries without ripping the lion's clothes.

Pros:
+Kids love it
+Great for teaching cause and effect
+Makes a lot of noise
+You can stick it on the window

Cons:
-Can be annoying for adults
-On/off switch and batteries are inconveniently located
-Isn't as fun if it's not stuck to a window
text_fidelity_b: Fisher-Price Roar 'n Ride Lion

text_fidelity_a:
Bézier Games Ultimate Werewolf Revised Edition Werewolf is not usually a "game night" game that you play with a group of friends. I've always used it in classroom settings, or with larger groups, usually upwards of 10 people, where this game really shines. Ultimately, Werewolf is a deduction game in which most players are Villagers, unwittingly being killed or eliminated by a sect of Werewolf players. Using very limited clues and knowledge, it's up to the Villagers to unmask the Werewolves and eliminate them from the game before they themselves are eaten.

The only real issue that I have with Werewolf is that there is player elimination, although since Werewolf is not a particularly long game, it's usually OK, and bystanders often have as much fun as the players.

There are plenty of versions of this game available out there, but I think that Bezier's "Ultimate" is certainly the way to go. The bits are durable and well made, and there are enough cards to play an 80 person game. That said, there is less content in here as compared to the "Revised Edition" that came out a few years ago. I still think that this is the box to get, however, as the roles and unique playing styles presented in the "Revised" box are more complicated, and not really in line with the casual spirit of the game. I think they certainly provide more variety, but at the expense of complicating the players and making it far more difficult for the moderator. As it's impossible to answer questions mid-game, it's best to leave the complicated roles to a different genre of game.

A 5-Star Product for sure.
text_fidelity_b: Bézier Games Ultimate Werewolf Revised Edition

The game comes with two sets of rules, a basic "family" set of rules and the advanced rules. Basic rules are fun, but the advanced rules is where the strategy comes in.

The premise is that you are a firefighter and you are rushing into the house to rescue people and animals. each person has a role that they play, but that can be switched during the game if another role would be more helpful. Overall, this game really fits the coop bill perfectly and it's been a hit in our family. I'd recommend it if you enjoy cooperative games and want to pretend you're a fire fighter!

text_fidelity_a:
32" Play Kitchen, 2 in 1 Toy Kitchen & Grill Playset Kitchen Pretend Play Toys Kitchen Playset Kids Kitchen Set with Cooking Accessories Pros: The kids love the kitchen playset, so much so that my 4.5-year-old niece preferred it to playing her favorite computer game for a full week and the 2-year-old couldn't be tempted away even by birthday cake. It's still the first toy she heads for when she visits. One kid can play on each side, so they can play at the same time. They didn't seem bothered that things didn't work quite right. I also like that they have whole food cooking ingredients (fruit, veggies, meat, eggs) rather than a bunch of finished foods or deserts.

Cons: The kitchen is basically held together by the parts having been firmly pressed into place. Thus, even lifting it by the roof can cause parts to come off. We've moved the kitchen around several times with no problem as long as you use the handles on the purple side panels. The oven and cupboard doors were initially hard to open, but luckily use has loosened this up some. The sink faucet pulls out during play, one of the BBQ-stick holders comes off very easily (when removing the stick to put food on or off), and some of the stickers don't want to stay on. Replacing the batteries is going to be a pain as they're on the underside of the cooking surface. The plastic food is a soft plastic, so the egg got crushed when stepped on. And cooking sure is noisy! I wish there was a way to lower the volume. So the adults feel like this isn't as good a product as it could be (3 stars) but the kids give it 5 stars.

ORIGINAL: This kitchen and grill playset is the perfect height for my two-year-old niece to play with. She likes to pretend like she is cooking, so she enjoys playing with the set. There is some assembly required, and the instructions are simply line drawings. Keep the box since looking at the two sides in the pictures is of more help in assembly than the instructions. Keep in mind that you will not fully tighten the joints until done with the first couple steps. The barbecue sign is a thin sheet of cardboard, so I assume that the thicker board is supposed to be put in the slot along with it. I don't know why they didn't just print the sign on the thicker board or even just past it on. As it is, you're trying to fit two separate sheets into a slot seemingly meant only for the thicker one. I had someone try to help me get it into the slot, but it was too tight to get in very far. I ended up cutting off some of the top just to make it fit (though it turns out I didn't need to do this. It could have just stuck up without running into anything). Except for this, assembly was not particularly difficult.

You use three AA batteries to power the sound. Once you hook up the spigot, you can put water in the sink and then pump it out through the spigot. The plastic food was recognizable as specific types of food, and the pots, plates, utensils, and bottles are distinct and fairly sturdy. Since it is merely pressure that fastens the joints together, this could come apart under especially hard play, but it's unlikely a two-year-old will cause any problems with it. Overall, I'm pleased and my niece is extremely happy to play with it when visiting my house.

UPDATE: The stickers are coming off after about a week, and not just because of use. They just didn't stick well to the water bottle and utensils. The handles on the cupboard about the oven is difficult to open because there's nothing to really get a grip on the handle. It's the perfect height for a 2-year-old, but my 4.5-year-old niece has to kneel to use it. (We wanted something small since we don't have lots of room to store the toys, but this maybe isn't something that will span a large age range.)
text_fidelity_b: 32" Play Kitchen, 2 in 1 Toy Kitchen & Grill Playset Kitchen Pretend Play Toys Kitchen Playset Kids Kitchen Set with Cooking Accessories

text_fidelity_a: Buffalo Games - Cinque Terre - 1000 Piece Jigsaw Puzzle This is a really well made puzzle. The artwork is great and the quality is exceptional. BUT, it is the most evil puzzle I have ever tried. Many of the mono-color pieces are interchangeable. The computer that designed the cuts might be able to tell the difference but I couldn't. There are (at least) 3 different ways to build the top row that  all seem correct. But then you move on to the second row, which is also mono-color(ish) and suffers from the same issue. So you find out that the top row is all wrong based on how the second row doesn't fit. So then you move onto the 3rd row - where the patterned pieces start AND THAT DOESN"T FIT WITH THE TOP TWO ROWS. So you end up rebuilding the second row based on the third row and the top row based on the now-reconstructed second row. It was maddening. Really, make it tough but only one solution please. Otherwise a very enjoyable puzzle and I'd definitely buy this brand again,

You think you are prepared for what the size of this set is, but I honestly had no idea how heavy it would be. Even before opening the box I thought, uh-oh, I may have miscalculated. And yes, I simply had no concept of how large over 4700 pieces was 😂🤣.

So I’ve been scoping out places in my house I might display this once I was done. Then I happened to be at the mall the other day and saw one in the display window at the Lego store and immediately tossed out all of my prior ideas because once I get this thing put together it’s going to be mammoth.

I’ll update my review if I encounter anything unexpected during my project, but so far it’s going as expected.

text_fidelity_a:
Harry Potter Lexicon-GO! Word Game Lexicon Go is a very fast-paced, easy-to-play word game using a deck of 52 plastic tiles, each with a letter of the alphabet. the tiles are arranged face down on the playing area, and each player draws 10 tiles from the deck. The goal is to arrange all 10 of your tiles into words as quickly as possible. If you're unable to use all of your letters to make words, you can swap out a tile (within certain parameters) or you can play on other players' words. The first player to use all 10 tiles wins the round. Win five rounds and you've won the game.

We played this game with two, three, four, and five adult players. I would guess that in at least 8 out of 10 rounds, one player was able to use all of her letters to form words without any swapping out or playing on another player's tiles -- which made the game move very, very quickly, , but also made it a little bit boring. There is very little strategizing and interaction. The best part was challenging words and learning the meaning of funny new words.

This was a little bit too fast-paced and frenetic for my tastes, and whether you could use all your tiles on the first draw depended primarily on getting a good vowel to consonant ratio- if you draw at least three vowels, it's pretty easy to make two, three, or four letter words to use all ten tiles. If you draw only one or two vowels, you will have a tough time using all your tiles.

The game is fun, clever, and well-made. The carrying case is well-made and the tiles are nice quality. This would be a great family game or vacation game, and it worked equally well with two players as it did with five players -- it just worked differently. It is versatile. If you're a fan of Scrabble or the New York Times crossword, this seems very fast-paced and a little too easy. It may better suited for younger players -- maybe elementary school-aged children.
text_fidelity_b: Harry Potter Lexicon-GO! Word Game

LEGO Hidden Side Graveyard Mystery 70420 Building Kit, App Toy for 7+ Year Old Boys and Girls, Interactive Augmented Reality Playset (335 Pieces) I hope they don't overdo it, but this new LEGO Augmented Reality system is quite cool.

There is an app that you download to your phone, and using that app, you can view your LEGO set, and watch it move and change a little bit. If you've seen someone playing Pokemon Go or using a filter on their camera phone, you'll get the idea. It works surprisingly well given that it's easy to slightly alter the design. The app itself is downloadable on iTunes and Android, and works well on the Android system, although you really likely want to use a phone because of the size of the tablet. It will work, but it gets in the way of play.

Like all parents, I'm not entirely thrilled about yet another excuse to hand over my phone, but I think that the augmented reality piece is really more of a gimmick that my daughter will tire of sooner rather than later. The building of the set must come first in order for this to work, and that's mildly educational, and we get to play with the LEGO set without the phone as well.

And did I mention how cool this set is, even without the augmented reality? The ghost theme makes for some cool pieces, and I like how this one looks when it's done. It's a winner.
text_fidelity_b: LEGO Hidden Side Graveyard Mystery 70420 Building Kit, App Toy for 7+ Year Old Boys and Girls, Interactive Augmented Reality Playset (335 Pieces)

text_fidelity_a:
All Things Equal, Inc. Loaded Questions [[VIDEOID:moOM6Q7TMDWRNW]]This is like an awesome mix between Apples to Apples and Trivial Pursuit. It's played very similarly to Apples to Apples, but you have an open-ended question, and everyone writes answers down on a piece of paper. Then the pieces of paper are handed in, and the person who is It has to guess who wrote what question. The person who is It gets one point per right answer that they match with the people playing the game.

It's a fun, and simple concept, which makes for a fun and simple game. And, the questions are awesome. I've gotten a few "getting to know you" books in the past, which have lists of supposedly interesting questions. All of those books pale in comparison to this awesome game. These questions are intense, interesting, and none of them put too much pressure on you.

My girlfriend and I found ourselves just reading the questions and answering them a lot, just by ourselves. It's a great way to talk about tons of different topics than the ones that usually come up. Like I said, these questions are great.

I usually really don't like party games like this. I usually like strategy games better. But this is one party game that I love.

Pros:
+Awesome questions
+Fun game
+Good quality
+Well designed

Cons:
-You need 4 people to play according to the rules, even though these are fun questions to ask if there are just two or three of you
text_fidelity_b: All Things Equal, Inc. Loaded Questions

Thames & Kosmos Wind Power V4.0 STEM Experiment Kit | Build a 3ft Wind Turbine to Generate Electricity | Learn About Renewable Energy & Power a Small Model Car | Weatherproof for Outdoor Use This kit was a lot more fun for Dad than it was for the kid. She's younger than the recommended age range, but had little trouble putting the whole model together in under 30 minutes with Dad's help. We barely used the book for assembly, but read the more educational "science" book cover to cover.

She and I talk all the time about renewable energy, largely because solar panels are looking like the next big home improvement project around here, and we get what I'd consider a reasonable amount of wind. She found the concepts easy enough to understand, and was interested to see what we'd be able to do in the backyard...and it's not much. The wind we got was not nearly enough to make this project effective, even on what I'd consider a relatively windy day. I put it on the roof for a short time and that helped, but not much. The turbine requires a battery, which makes both of us question where the small amount of power we are generating actually comes from.

So the experiments died off rather quickly, and this became a very short model building project for her that Dad is enjoying tinkering with to see if he can charge one of those rechargable cell-phone batteries. Kid is off playing with the very small toy car that comes with the kit, but doesn't look like it belongs at all.

If you get a lot of wind, then it's probably a lot more fun, but it's for the younger age of the spectrum for sure.
text_fidelity_b: Thames & Kosmos Wind Power V4.0 STEM Experiment Kit | Build a 3ft Wind Turbine to Generate Electricity | Learn About Renewable Energy & Power a Small Model Car | Weatherproof for Outdoor Use

text_fidelity_a: Crayola 18ct Twistables Colored Pencils (2 Pack) These twistable pencils came in superb packaging and thus arrived in great condition, none broken, pencils and their boxes in excellent condition.  These twistables, while not as bright as regular colored pencils, are really a nice option to standard colored pencils.  They are more portable in that you don't have to always carry a pencil sharpener or worry about emptying shavings.  They just wear down like crayons, but since the lead is in plastic casing you don't have to keep tearing the paper away like you do with crayons.  These are excellent for children and also for seniors or anyone who doesn't have a lot of strength in their hands, or who struggles with sharpening pencils.  Unfortunately being soft lead, the leads do wear down a bit faster.  Overall these are nice pencils to have on hand.

Repos JUST01 Just One, Various There are a lot of "just one word clues" games out there, from Codenames and Decrypto to games like Funglish, Crosstalk or Word Slam, and this game is yet another to add to that group. I think, however, that it's my secnd favorite of the bunch, and if you need a Codenames Killer, this might be up your alley.

In this team game, one player is attempting to guess a word that the rest of their team knows. Each team member writes down one word only, then compares to see if any matches are detected. If they are, those cards are discarded, and the guesser is left with fewer clues. Therefore, the more obtuse clues you get, the more you'll have, but it can be more difficult to deduce the word than if you're given a few obvious clues.

What I like about this game is that it manages to be a louder than usual team game with secrets. In Codenames or Crosstalk, two previous iterations of the concept, games are fun, but often it's players staring at the board in silence. In this one, you still can't say much, but it does lend itself to quicker play, and it's easier to communicate more freely once you have your clues written since your work is done, and the stress of the round is over for the clue-givers. This is a hard game, and it's definitely a word game, but lends itself to being an excellent family gathering game.
text_fidelity_b: Repos JUST01 Just One, Various

This one in particular has the highest age range of the three games, going 12-100, which is a little high, although I do believe the clues are a little more difficult to decipher in this set than the others, which I figured should range at the 7 or 8 to adult age range.

This set is far more thematic than the others, having clues that very specifically fit into the theme - adventure, fantasy, sci-fi and superheroes - which is a good concept. Other sets have tried this, but didn't have enough questions to ensure that the theme carried through.
